description:
v2AwaitCallback's main-thread branch cannot receive a callback delivered on the main dispatch queue. WKWebView.evaluateJavaScript delivers completion handlers exactly that way, so EVERY browser JS eval reaching that branch is guaranteed to fail: it burns its full timeout, then returns nil. While burning it, it holds the main queue — and socket commands reach their work via v2MainSync — so each failing browser command freezes the entire CLI/socket control plane and the UI for the full timeout.

Code is BYTE-IDENTICAL at v0.61.0 (the build that wedged) and release/v0.64.0 (current). Not a stale-build problem — it ships today. Blocks next production release.

PROVEN by repro harness at tools/await-wedge-repro/ (run.sh):
  timer     (CFRunLoop timer source)        -> callback FIRES,      0.50s
  mainqueue (DispatchQueue.main.async)      -> callback NEVER runs, 3.00s -> nil
  never     (never invoked)                 -> 3.00s -> nil
Same code, same nesting, only delivery path differs. A nested CFRunLoopRunInMode inside an in-progress _dispatch_main_queue_drain cannot drain main-queue blocks; libdispatch will not re-enter a drain already on the stack.

This falsifies the shipped comment at BrowserHandlers.swift:321-324 ('The loop still pumps events (WebKit completion callbacks, rendering, main-queue blocks), so main is not frozen'). Those are precisely what it does NOT pump.

PRODUCTION INCIDENT 2026-08-12: ~53-agent Marquee V2 fleet running browser-proof gates. Main thread stalled 25+ min continuous and monotonic, longest fleet timeout 60s. UI dead, every c11 CLI call died at its 10s client timeout, event stream froze. Agents themselves unaffected (28/53 measurably advancing, PTYs draining). Immune to killing the WebContent process (termination error is itself main-queue delivered) and to lldb (hardened runtime + SIP).

REAL-WORLD RATE, agent transcripts 2026-08-12: 205 'timeout: method=browser' + 29 'Condition not met before timeout' + 3 'Timed out waiting for JavaScript result' = 237 failures in one day. CLI abandons at 10s while server keeps burning its timeout, so these are largely invisible in ps and read as agent flakiness.

NOT YET EXPLAINED: repro shows the deadline loop DOES unwind on time, so one stuck await cannot explain a 25-min stall. Leading hypothesis is a serialized backlog of failing commands (agents retry after 10s CLI timeout, refilling faster than drain). SIGSTOPing all 55 agents for 4 min did not drain it — likely too short for a 20-min backlog, but unconfirmed. NEXT STEP: freeze all agents 20-30 min and watch stalledMs. Plateau = backlog confirmed and wedge is self-healing given quiet; still climbing with zero agents = a second defect.

FIXES:
1. Do not await a main-queue-delivered callback from inside a main-queue drain. Keep the JS-eval await off the main-thread branch, or make the socket command complete asynchronously instead of blocking main. Root fix; rest is mitigation.
2. Cap timeout_ms (BrowserHandlers.swift:1357 is lower-bounded only: max(1, ... ?? 5_000)). Uncapped value is a direct multiplier on control-plane downtime.
3. Correct the comment at BrowserHandlers.swift:321-324 — it documents behavior the implementation lacks.
4. Fail fast when the WKWebView has no committed document instead of burning the timeout.

RELATED, BOTH UNMERGED (in neither main nor release/v0.64.0) — assess together before release:
  origin/fix/C11-198-runloop-idle  'stops swallowing nested run loops' (2026-08-10)
  origin/fix/C11-204-modal-wedge   'browser modals never go app-modal' (2026-08-11); per CLAUDE.md the insecure-HTTP prompt held main up to 6.8h. Fleet drives proofs against http://127.0.0.1, exactly that path.

INSTRUMENTATION: MainThreadHangMonitor worked well (C11-192 fingerprinting attributed the stall correctly). Two gaps: hang.log grew ~23MB/min to 212MB (needs rotation/cap; ~1.3GB/hr sustained), and seven precursor episodes (2.4s-10.7s) never surfaced to the operator — a repeated-fingerprint signal would have flagged this before it went terminal.

Full writeup: docs/c11-browser-await-main-wedge.md
